economy.summary: His campaign site says he pushed for property, sales, and income tax relief to make living more affordable and calls for policies that expand economic opportunities, not government.
economy.short: Pushed property, sales, income tax relief; expand economic opportunities.

taxes.summary: Says he has never voted to raise taxes on his neighbors and prioritizes reining in state spending, and advocates the Responsible Budgeting Act to mandate on-time budgets based on actual revenue rather than political wish lists.
taxes.short: Says never voted to raise taxes; backs Responsible Budgeting Act.

abortion.summary: His state House member website lists upholding the sanctity of life as one of his five main emphasis areas as a legislator; his Senate campaign site does not detail an abortion position.
abortion.short: Lists upholding the sanctity of life among legislative emphasis areas.

education.summary: His campaign site says he will ensure education dollars fund students, not bureaucratic systems, and commits to giving parents a stronger voice in their children's education.
education.short: Says education dollars should fund students; stronger parent voice.

healthcare.summary: His campaign site proposes expanding healthcare options for consumers that lower costs and deliver quality care.
healthcare.short: Proposes expanding healthcare options that lower costs, deliver quality.

energy.summary: His campaign site says he opposed new taxes on energy, fought against utility rate hikes, and fought to preserve open space and farmland against what it calls runaway data center growth.
energy.short: Opposed new energy taxes, utility hikes; limits data center growth.

guns.summary: His state House member website lists protecting Second Amendment rights as one of his five main emphasis areas as a legislator; his Senate campaign site does not detail a gun-policy position.
guns.short: Lists protecting Second Amendment rights among legislative emphasis areas.

economy.summary: His campaign priorities page says he is focused on lowering the costs of everyday essentials, expanding access to affordable housing, and supporting policies that make life more affordable for working people.
economy.short: Focuses on lowering everyday costs, expanding affordable housing access.

taxes.summary: Applauded passage of the 2026-2027 state budget, calling it a responsible spending plan, and cited its $1 billion in property tax relief for homeowners and an expanded Working Pennsylvanians Tax Credit.
taxes.short: Applauded 2026-27 budget; cites property tax relief, expanded credit.

abortion.summary: Was endorsed in the 2025 special election by Planned Parenthood Pennsylvania PAC, which backs candidates who support access to reproductive health care including abortion; the Pennsylvania Choice Tracker reports no direct public statements from him on abortion.
abortion.short: Endorsed by Planned Parenthood PAC; no direct statements documented.

education.summary: His campaign priorities page says every student deserves a safe, high-quality education, cites his work for fair public school funding, and says he passed protections requiring schools to report digital harassment and exploitation incidents.
education.short: Supports fair public school funding; passed school safety protections.

healthcare.summary: His campaign priorities page says he is committed to addressing healthcare costs for families and to lowering healthcare expenses for seniors.
healthcare.short: Committed to addressing healthcare costs for families and seniors.

energy.summary: His campaign priorities page emphasizes preserving forests, farmland, waterways, and hunting and fishing heritage, and supports responsible conservation and expanded Sunday hunting; it does not detail an energy policy.
energy.short: Supports conservation of forests, farmland, waterways; Sunday hunting.

guns.summary: His campaign priorities page says first responders should have the tools they need to keep communities safe; it does not detail a position on gun policy.
guns.short: Supports resources for first responders; no gun-policy details given.
